span.label: The forms memory takes, the brain systems that support each, and the synaptic mechanisms common to all of them.
span.quote: Memory is the record of experience represented in the brain.

span.label: existence
span.quote: There are multiple forms of memory supported by distinct brain systems.

span.label: memory
span.quote: Memory is the record of experience represented in the brain.

span.label: review
span.quote: Thus a central tenet in this field is that there are multiple memory systems , each characterized by distinct operating characteristics and brain pathways in which memories are embodied in the plasticity of information processing within the relevant neural circuit (Figure 1; Eichenbaum & Cohen, 2001).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Coincident excitatory input and depolarization at NMDA receptors admits Ca++, triggering a cAMP-CREB-immediate-early-gene-protein-synthesis cascade that structurally fixes the synaptic change
span.quote: LTP is typically induced by the co-occurence of excitatory input and intracellular depolarization at the so-called Hebbian synapse , involving N-methyl-d-aspartate (NMDA) receptors that allow the entry of Ca++ into the synapse, which activates cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Repeated two-way medial-temporal-cortical interactions (including replay) progressively reorganize connections among cortical representations, consolidating episodes and semantic knowledge into permanent storage
span.quote: Over a prolonged period, these interactions result in a substantial reorganization and consolidation of connections among cortical representations to incorporate the information contained in new episodes and abstracted semantic knowledge into permanent memory (McClelland et al., 1995).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Emotional arousal releases glucocorticoids and engages adrenergic mechanisms through the amygdala, which modulates the strength of memory fixation in other memory systems
span.quote: Emotional arousal induces the release of glucocorticoids and adrenergic mechanisms via the amygdala, influencing memory fixation in both the declarative and procedural memory systems and in both animals and humans.

span.label: The medial temporal lobe converts short-term into long-term memory without being the permanent store, which is why H.M. lost new memories and kept old ones
span.quote: Furthermore, the fact that H.M. retains memories for events that occurred remotely prior to his surgery indicated that these brain areas are not the site of permanent storage but instead play a role in the organization and permanent storage of memories elsewhere in the brain through the process known as memory consolidation .

span.label: Declarative memory works by binding items to each other, to their context and to neighbouring events, which is what makes it relational
span.quote: Furthermore, this system is characterized by relational memory processing, in which items to be remembered are bound to associated items, to the context in which the experience occurred, to preceding and succeeding events, and to related memories (Cohen et al., 1997; Eichenbaum, 2004).

span.label: False memory is a failure of that same relational machinery rather than a separate defect - the network returns relations that never occurred
span.quote: Notably, false memory typically involves an error of relational processing that retrieves relations that did not actually occur but is embodied in the network of relational memories.

span.label: Long-term potentiation runs through a molecular cascade ending in protein synthesis, and blocking any step blocks permanent memory
span.quote: Evidence that the permanent fixation of memories depends on this molecular and cellular cascade of events comes from studies showing that memory fixation can be halted by interference with the molecules in this cascade.

span.label: The timing of that blockade separates the two kinds of memory: it stops permanent fixation and leaves initial learning and short-term memory intact
span.quote: These treatments are effective when given before or within minutes after learning, and but are not effective if they are delayed, indicating that the molecular cascade leading to protein synthesis is not essential to initial learning or to maintaining short-term memory, but is essential for permanent memory fixation.

span.label: Potentiation and depression share a molecular substrate and differ only in the timing rules of synaptic activity
span.quote: LTD involves the same molecular substrates as LTP but occurs with different timing rules of activity at synapses.

span.label: The foundational evidence for the whole framework rests on a single surgical patient
span.note: what this limits: the empirical base of the whole systems framework: it begins with THE STUDY OF A PATIENT KNOWN BY HIS INITIALS H.M. - a single surgical case
span.quote: A major breakthrough in understanding memory systems and their underlying brain mechanisms began with the study of a patient known by his initials H.M. (HM Patient; Scoville & Milner, 1957).

span.label: The systems are described as distinct while also interacting and storing the same event separately, so the boundaries are functional rather than sharp
span.note: what this limits: any claim that the memory systems are separable: THE PROCEDURAL AND EMOTIONAL MEMORY SYSTEMS CAN STORE AND DISTINCTLY EXPRESS DIFFERENT FORMS OF MEMORY EVEN FOR THE SAME EVENT - distinct and simultaneously overlapping
span.quote: Thus, in addition to the declarative memory system, the procedural and emotional memory systems can store and distinctly express different forms of memory even for the same event.

span.label: Implicit memory is characterised as a variety of systems rather than one, so the category is defined by what it is not
span.note: what this limits: the category implicit memory itself: THESE VARIOUS FORMS OF IMPLICIT MEMORY ARE SUPPORTED BY A VARIETY OF MEMORY SYSTEMS - it is not one system but the residue left when declarative memory is removed
span.quote: These various forms of implicit memory are supported by a variety of memory systems and within the cerebral cortex, as in the case of priming introduced above.

span.label: long-term potentiation
span.quote: An important model in the study of the cellular basis of memory is the phenomenon of long-term potentiation (LTP), a long-lasting increase in the strength of a synaptic response following stimulation (Bliss et al., 2007).

span.label: associative memory
span.quote: There is a large variety of forms of memory beginning with elementary and non-associative types of memory, including habituation and sensitization, and reaching the most complex forms of associative memory , including episodic memory and semantic memory.

span.label: memory - divided by DURATION: whether it lasts a short or a long period
span.quote: Specific forms of memory are characterized by whether they last a short or long period, by whether they involve unique experiences or accumulated knowledge, and by whether memory is expressed explicitly by conscious remembering or implicitly through changes in the speed or bias of performance in particular tasks.

span.label: memory - divided by EXPRESSION: explicit conscious remembering versus implicit change in speed or bias
span.quote: Whereas H.M. and amnesic patients can be severely impaired in declarative memory, they typically retain various forms of implicit memory , which involves the ability to acquire skills, habits, and preferences that can be expressed by improved performance or altered bias without conscious recollection (Schacter, 1987).

span.label: memory - divided by CONTENT: unique experiences versus accumulated knowledge, the episodic/semantic axis
span.quote: The medial temporal lobe is critical to the processing and storage of episodic memories , our memories of specific personal experiences that happened at a particular place and time (Baddeley et al., 2002).

span.label: short-term memory - as working memory: explicitly a form of DECLARATIVE memory, held in consciousness
span.quote: Some of this information also enters working memory , a form of declarative memory that enables us to transiently retain and manipulate the information “on-line” in consciousness (Dobbins et al., 2002).

span.label: implicit memory - as a family of LONG-term systems: procedural, emotional and priming, each with its own pathway
span.quote: Thus, in addition to the declarative memory system, the procedural and emotional memory systems can store and distinctly express different forms of memory even for the same event.

span.label: recognition - familiarity versus recollection: two capacities of one cortical-hippocampal system
span.quote: The cortical-hippocampal system supports both our capacity for a sense of familiarity with previous exposure to specific stimuli and the ability for active recollection of prior experiences.

span.quote: A major breakthrough in understanding memory systems and their underlying brain mechanisms began with the study of a patient known by his initials H.M. (HM Patient; Scoville & Milner, 1957).

span.label: supports → Schacter's characterisation of implicit memory
span.quote: which involves the ability to acquire skills, habits, and preferences that can be expressed by improved performance or altered bias without conscious recollection (Schacter, 1987)

span.label: extends → Eichenbaum and Cohen's multiple-memory-systems framework
span.quote: Thus a central tenet in this field is that there are multiple memory systems , each characterized by distinct operating characteristics and brain pathways in which memories are embodied in the plasticity of information processing within the relevant neural circuit (Figure 1; Eichenbaum & Cohen, 2001).

span.label: working memory —is-a→ declarative memory
span.quote: Some of this information also enters working memory , a form of declarative memory that enables us to transiently retain and manipulate the information “on-line” in consciousness (Dobbins et al., 2002).

span.label: procedural memory —is-a→ implicit memory
span.quote: One implicit memory system involves cortical areas interacting with the striatum in support of procedural memory , the acquisition of skilled behavior and acquired habits.

span.label: emotional memory —is-a→ implicit memory
span.quote: Another distinct memory system involves cortical and subcortical areas interacting with the amygdala to support the attachment of affective significance to otherwise neutral stimuli and events.

span.label: declarative memory —distinct-from→ implicit memory
span.quote: Whereas H.M. and amnesic patients can be severely impaired in declarative memory, they typically retain various forms of implicit memory , which involves the ability to acquire skills, habits, and preferences that can be expressed by improved performance or altered bias without conscious recollection (Schacter, 1987).

span.label: medial temporal lobe —causes→ memory consolidation
span.quote: From these observations researchers concluded that the parts of the medial temporal lobe that were removed in H.M, including the hippocampus and adjacent parahippocampal region, play a critical role in converting a short-term memory to a long-term, permanent memory store.

span.label: hippocampus —part-of→ medial temporal lobe
span.quote: From these observations researchers concluded that the parts of the medial temporal lobe that were removed in H.M, including the hippocampus and adjacent parahippocampal region, play a critical role in converting a short-term memory to a long-term, permanent memory store.

span.label: relational memory processing —causes→ false memory
span.quote: Notably, false memory typically involves an error of relational processing that retrieves relations that did not actually occur but is embodied in the network of relational memories.

span.label: long-term potentiation —part-of→ Hebbian synapse
span.quote: LTP is typically induced by the co-occurence of excitatory input and intracellular depolarization at the so-called Hebbian synapse , involving N-methyl-d-aspartate (NMDA) receptors that allow the entry of Ca++ into the synapse, which activates cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP).

span.label: long term depression —contrasted-with→ long-term potentiation
span.quote: LTD involves the same molecular substrates as LTP but occurs with different timing rules of activity at synapses.

span.label: long-term potentiation —causes→ memory consolidation
span.quote: Thus, a series of molecular reactions plays a vital role in fixating the changes in synaptic function that occur in LTP.

span.label: habituation —part-of→ multiple memory systems
span.quote: There is a large variety of forms of memory beginning with elementary and non-associative types of memory, including habituation and sensitization, and reaching the most complex forms of associative memory , including episodic memory and semantic memory.

span.label: familiarity —distinct-from→ recollection
span.quote: The cortical-hippocampal system supports both our capacity for a sense of familiarity with previous exposure to specific stimuli and the ability for active recollection of prior experiences.

span.label: iconic memory —contrasted-with→ working memory
span.quote: Information from new experiences initially is stored in iconic memory and forms of short term memory that can support brief storage and immediate recall of substantial detail.

span.label: episodic memory —is-a→ associative memory
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — REPLACES concept_edges[1], which typed episodic memory as a kind of DECLARATIVE memory. That is true of the field and this paper does not say it: the only sentence in the staged body placing episodic memory under a superclass places it under ASSOCIATIVE memory. The old edge is withdrawn, not corrected in place, because its `to` was wrong rather than its quote. NO `relation`/`relation_evidence` ON THIS EDGE, DELIBERATELY: the sentence's class cue is `the most complex FORMS OF associative memory`, and the gate's is-a cue list holds `a form of` but not `forms of`. That is Q-1201 exactly - the cue vocabulary lacks the plural of a form it already accepts - and I am not editing the cue lists, which have two named amenders. The edge therefore joins the 92% that carry a span and no marked clause. Add the clause when the vocabulary is widened.
span.quote: There is a large variety of forms of memory beginning with elementary and non-associative types of memory, including habituation and sensitization, and reaching the most complex forms of associative memory , including episodic memory and semantic memory.

span.label: Across all its varieties, memory is claimed to reduce to changes in synaptic connections inside the circuits of each memory system.
span.quote: All forms of memory are based on changes in synaptic connections within neural circuits of each memory system.

span.label: Blocking the molecular cascade only works within minutes of learning, which shows the cascade is needed for permanent fixation but not for initial or short-term memory.
span.quote: These treatments are effective when given before or within minutes after learning, and but are not effective if they are delayed, indicating that the molecular cascade leading to protein synthesis is not essential to initial learning or to maintaining short-term memory, but is essential for permanent memory fixation.

span.label: Episodic memory is the form most prominently impaired by aging, even though all types of learning capacity decline somewhat.
span.quote: Although aging causes amnesia involving some loss of all types of learning capacity, the most common and most prominent decline is in episodic memory (Wilson et al., 2006).

span.label: Age-related memory loss is attributed to fewer synaptic connections and weakened neuromodulation rather than to neuronal death.
span.quote: Normal aging is not caused by the loss of neurons, but rather by decreases in the number of synaptic connections and in loss of neuromodulation that normally activates and coordinates processing in these brain areas, particularly involving pathways that use the neurotransmitter acetylcholine .

span.label: False memory is characterised as a failure of relational processing that retrieves relations which never occurred but are supported by the relational network.
span.quote: Notably, false memory typically involves an error of relational processing that retrieves relations that did not actually occur but is embodied in the network of relational memories.

span.label: H.M. retained childhood memories while losing the ability to form new ones, separating storage from consolidation
span.quote: Despite his inability to remember new information, H.M. has considerable intact memories from his childhood and information obtained up to a few years before his surgery.

span.label: blocking the molecular cascade prevents permanent memory while leaving initial learning and short-term memory intact
span.quote: These treatments are effective when given before or within minutes after learning, and but are not effective if they are delayed, indicating that the molecular cascade leading to protein synthesis is not essential to initial learning or to maintaining short-term memory, but is essential for permanent memory fixation.

span.label: amnesic patients impaired in declarative memory typically retain implicit memory
span.quote: Whereas H.M. and amnesic patients can be severely impaired in declarative memory, they typically retain various forms of implicit memory , which involves the ability to acquire skills, habits, and preferences that can be expressed by improved performance or altered bias without conscious recollection (Schacter, 1987).

span.label: potentiation and depression occur in every structure known to take part in memory
span.quote: LTP and LTD occur among all brain structures that are known to participate in different kinds of memory.

span.label: memory
span.quote: Memory is the record of experience represented in the brain.

span.label: multiple memory systems
span.quote: Thus a central tenet in this field is that there are multiple memory systems , each characterized by distinct operating characteristics and brain pathways in which memories are embodied in the plasticity of information processing within the relevant neural circuit (Figure 1; Eichenbaum & Cohen, 2001).

span.label: learning
span.quote: Importantly, the topic of memory is closely related to learning , which is the process by which memories are obtained, and learning is not exclusive to but includes various forms of conditioning and reinforcement learning , both of which are also covered as major topical areas in Scholarpedia .

span.label: declarative memory
span.quote: Studies using functional brain imaging have confirmed that the hippocampus and parahippocampal region are activated during the encoding and retrieval of memories in humans, and these studies have also identified a large network of areas in the cerebral cortex that work together to support declarative memory , our ability for learning and consciously remembering everyday facts and events (Squire et al., 2004).

span.label: working memory
span.quote: Some of this information also enters working memory , a form of declarative memory that enables us to transiently retain and manipulate the information “on-line” in consciousness (Dobbins et al., 2002).

span.label: episodic memory
span.quote: The medial temporal lobe is critical to the processing and storage of episodic memories , our memories of specific personal experiences that happened at a particular place and time (Baddeley et al., 2002).

span.label: semantic memory
span.quote: Our permanent storehouse of memories, called semantic memory , involves a large distributed network of cortical areas that are involved in the perception, action, and analysis of the material being learned.

span.label: implicit memory
span.quote: Whereas H.M. and amnesic patients can be severely impaired in declarative memory, they typically retain various forms of implicit memory , which involves the ability to acquire skills, habits, and preferences that can be expressed by improved performance or altered bias without conscious recollection (Schacter, 1987).

span.label: priming
span.quote: In addition, specific representations in these cortical areas can be shaped by training, allowing for the learning of perceptual skills (Karni, 1996), and are subject to a biasing towards non-conscious retrieval of recently experienced perceptions, called priming (Schacter & Buckner, 1998).

span.label: procedural memory
span.quote: One implicit memory system involves cortical areas interacting with the striatum in support of procedural memory , the acquisition of skilled behavior and acquired habits.

span.label: memory consolidation
span.quote: Furthermore, the fact that H.M. retains memories for events that occurred remotely prior to his surgery indicated that these brain areas are not the site of permanent storage but instead play a role in the organization and permanent storage of memories elsewhere in the brain through the process known as memory consolidation .

span.label: relational memory processing
span.quote: Furthermore, this system is characterized by relational memory processing, in which items to be remembered are bound to associated items, to the context in which the experience occurred, to preceding and succeeding events, and to related memories (Cohen et al., 1997; Eichenbaum, 2004).

span.label: long-term potentiation (LTP)
span.quote: An important model in the study of the cellular basis of memory is the phenomenon of long-term potentiation (LTP), a long-lasting increase in the strength of a synaptic response following stimulation (Bliss et al., 2007).

span.label: long term depression (LTD)
span.quote: In addition to LTP, there is also mechanism that diminishes the strength of connections at infrequently used synapses called long term depression (LTD).

span.label: flashbulb memories
span.quote: Thus, emotionally intense experiences can lead to more vivid and lasting declarative memories, sometimes called flashbulb memories, and to deeply seated habits.
